recipes.name: Herb-Glazed Roasted Turkey
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 pound) whole turkey, neck and giblets removed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Rinse turkey, then pat thoroughly dry with paper towels. Brush turkey with extra-virgin olive oil, inside and out.
Mix together 1 teaspoon salt, thyme, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper in a small bowl; sprinkle all over turkey. Place turkey on a rack set in a roasting pan.
Roast turkey in the preheated oven for 2 hours.
While turkey is roasting, stir together honey, melted butter, parsley, sage, basil, remaining 1 teaspoon salt, and remaining 1 teaspoon pepper in a medium bowl until glaze is smooth and well blended.

Brush some of the glaze over turkey. Continue roasting turkey, basting frequently with remaining glaze, until no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, about 2 more hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh, near the bone, should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Remove turkey from the oven, cover with a doubled sheet of aluminum foil, and allow to rest in a warm area before slicing, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Herb-Glazed Roasted Turkey
raw_recipe.description: This glazed turkey recipe features a whole roasted bird, brushed and basted with a honey-butter glaze flavored with parsley, thyme, sage, and basil.

review.reviewBody: This recipe by Moira is actually my mom!! Hi mom!! Of course we are an italian family and my mom can obviously cook like no other but I am not a fan of cooking, however this year we were not going to be together so I decided I was going to cook my first turkey ever and I used this recipe. IT WAS AMAZAING!!! I followed the instructions exactly as my mom instructed and it came out so tender, so perfectly cooked! I am going to make this turkey again on Christmas day!! THE BEST TURKEY EVER!

Very moist and flavorful turkey. I used a cooking bag and altered the time as follows: only one hour instead of two before adding the honey, then add the honey mixture and cook until done, roughly 2 1/2 hours. I also opened the bag only once to baste the turkey after I put the honey mixture on.

I didn't have any sage, so I substituted oregano. I was a little worried about the seasonings being so strong, but the flavor was not over-powering at all. Even my boyfriend, who dislikes heavily-seasoned food, loved it. Thank you for this recipe. I will definitely make this again!

I decided to try something different and it paid off! After reading all these great reviews, I decided on this one, the only thing I got from another recipe was to put butter under the skin on each side of the Turkey, between the skin and breast. It came out absolutely perfect! Plus all the ingredients were ingredients that most everyone already has! Thank you!

I did this for my first time cooking a turkey and it came out delicious! I followed the suggestion to cut the honey 50/50 with karo and it was perfect. Since then, I've learned to do the following with it (coping from an email to a family member) -- 

I use ground sage, ground parsley, raw honey, and I cut the honey 50/50 with karo. 

Brush the bird liberally with the oil. Liberally dust the bird with the herbs in step 2. I usually pat/rub the herbs into it and make sure the bird is pretty well covered with them. Make sure you get under the wings and on all sides of the bird.

Don't put the bird in a bag, but cover it with aluminum foil. Try to avoid opening the oven except to pull it out and brush it with glaze. (We have a gas oven).

We brush the bird about every 30 minutes while it's cooking until it's done.

Note: If you scale the recipe to the poundage of bird you have, you'll be drowning in glaze. What I do is scale it up for the first part, then I cut all the other stuff (needed in step 4 for the glaze) in half from there. I still have glaze left over, but I'm not wasting a ton of ingredients and it's much easier to manage mixing everything together.

made this 2 yrs in a row. same guests. absolutely love it.

funny enough, 1st time.i made the turkey upside down. yeah. new to this.
anyway, the turkey came out so moist and tender.. where the white meat can be dry, i had none.
actually requested i do that again!! but i made this yrs proper side up, and still was.just as good!

My turkey came out beautifully! I didn't have enough honey so I substituted half the honey with maple syrup. I think the color was darker because of the syrup. I used dried herbs, not fresh. I did prep my turkey by rubbing butter under the skin & used butter on the outside instead of olive oil.
My family loved this! I used a roasting bag that was also helpful. I would recommend getting the drippings before you use the glaze. The glaze will make the drippings too sweet.

I just started taking over Thanksgiving dinners for the last few yrs.- & since then have tried a different recipe every year, looking for that special one to make mine. I'm certain I found it this yr., especially after hearing my son say "Mom, this is the one!" AND there were absolutely no left overs! It was the most delicious turkey I had ever tasted- juicy inside, light & mildly crispy outside! Even my Mom said it was the best! The only thing I added was a stick of sweet butter, rubbed under the skin- that's it. After all my research on cooking turkeys, I kept on reading that placing butter under the skin would assist in creating a juicy bird. Well it definitely did and this is definitely a keeper!!

This was very good! All of the ingredients are on hand already...I did, however, also inject my turkey with Texas Butter (spicier butter) and then after 2 hours of the turkey roasting I basted it about 4 times. The turkey was incredibly moist. Key point, I think, is to make sure that you pat the turkey dry and then to really rub it down with olive oil as the first step.

This is one of the best turkeys I have had in a very long time. The only thing I added was some turky stock in the roasting pan and a lemon and orange in the cavaity while roasting. It turned out so well I was highly impressed. Will use this recipe next year, and the years after that...it's a keeper!

So if your a purist who thinks too many changes to a recipe bastardizes it, keep scrolling. If you like improvising with what you got, read on. So, I had many of the spices, but in combos, such as poultry & Italian seasoning. Also thought I had dried parsley, but it was cilantro. Also reduced honey by half. Despite these substitutions, it turned out great. There are literally no leftovers. Everyone took a plate!

This recipe was FANTASTIC! I didn't change a thing. Our Thanksgiving turkey was the best ever. Thank you!
Still a favorite year after year!
